analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. The patch touches two spots, both in the add-on hold settings table near lines 157-161. The first edits the DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET row to say that every build reads the variable, even though it is intended for tests only. The second renames the settle-bound constant to addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault and notes that a load still running after the bound is waited for, not abandoned. I examined the supplied head excerpts (lines 307-601 of the file), which are unchanged context. They cover the cache, SSD prefix cache, env-variable and model verification sections. They do not include the changed table lines, so I judged those from the patch alone.

No code, endpoint or control changes. The statement that every build reads DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET is documentation that discloses existing behavior, and it is relevant to TB-012, T-059 and A-018. It does not itself introduce a vulnerability. It does flag that a release build honors an environment override for the hold socket path. The surrounding text says the variable is not in the LaunchAgent passthrough list, so the installed provider always serves the default socket. This may deserve a check that the override cannot be used by a same-UID process to redirect the socket. That would be a pre-existing design question in AddonHoldPaths.swift, not something this PR introduced, and the code is not supplied. The settle-bound note that a running load is waited for rather than abandoned affects availability semantics, because a hold can wait on a long model load. That relates to T-059 and A-018, and I cannot verify it without the Swift source (ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift).

I found no concrete regression and no threat-model invalidation. Remaining questions for integration: whether the code matches the documented release-build read of DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET, and whether the settle wait is bounded in practice.
